> # I just wanted to check the column names
> # Description of the study: This study looked at sex differences in sleep patterns in mice, especially in REM-like sleep. The researchers found that female mice actually slept less than males but had more REM-like sleep. They also showed that if you only look at group averages without checking for sex differences, you can miss some major findings. The paper makes a strong case for always including and analyzing sex as a variable in sleep studies. It’s a good example of how statistical analysis can help uncover biological differences that would otherwise be hidden or overlooked. 
> # My statistical replications: I'd like to replicate the box plot for how minutes of sleep and wake differed between sexes during both the light and dark periods. For the summary stats I replicate the true means of simulated total sleep minutes between female and male mice in the control and treatment groups. For my model replicion portion I choose to replicate a model where the researchers Disaggregated by sex and modeled a sex × treatment interaction on simulated sleep data from a hypothetical control versus treatment study where there were unequal sample sizes accurately estimates the true means but failed to detect the true treatment effect (box plot). 
> # To read my data file into R, I simply was able to access a csv. file from Dryad and I was able to upload that to GitHub and upload the raw version into R, making it usable to me to manipulate.

> # After finding the true means for my summary stat replication, I can replicate all sex × treatment-specific 95% confidence intervals and see if by that model the true means are included in the interval for the inferential statistic replication portion.
> # Summary stats with 95% confidence intervals for each Sex × Cohort group
> ci_stats <- data %>%
+     group_by(Sex, Cohort) %>%
+     summarise(
+         mean_total_sleep = mean(total_min, na.rm = TRUE),
+         sd_total_sleep = sd(total_min, na.rm = TRUE),
+         n = n(),
+         se = sd_total_sleep / sqrt(n),
+         lower_95_CI = mean_total_sleep - qnorm(0.975) * se,
+         upper_95_CI = mean_total_sleep + qnorm(0.975) * se,
+         .groups = "drop"
+     )
> 
> print(ci_stats)
